newsitem.title: ITALY: GOLF-ROMERO LEADS DESPITE TWO-SHOT PENALTY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ROMERO LEADS DESPITE TWO-SHOT PENALTY.

text.p: Argentina's Eduardo Romero led the Italian Open at the halfway stage on Friday despite incurring a two-stroke penalty when he played his first round.
The 42-year-old Romero, who won the Italian title in 1994, had the penalty imposed when his playing partners reported that he had grounded his putter on his line during a practice putt.
Romero made up the strokes and picked up another for good measure as he carded a three-under-par 69 to move seven under on 137 and into a one-shot lead.
Sweden's Patrik Sjoland, who ran up a triple bogey after another curious penalty incident, and Englishmen Gordon Brand and Brian Davis were Romero's closest pursuers.

The previous day's events served to unsettle leader Romero but he then shrugged off the two penalty shots to pick up three birdies. In two rounds he has collected nine birdies without dropping any strokes other than his penalty.
"I was worried at the start that I might not be able to get the penalty out of my mind," said Romero.

"I trusted my playing partner the day before, Carl Mason, who reported that I had touched the line of my putt, even though I couldn't remember doing it. So I just had to get on with things and try to forget it.
"When I did, I went back to playing the fantastic golf I'm now capable of since changing my swing with my teaching uncle Mario Romero, who's also helped me with my putting stroke.
"...maybe I can win now, even with the penalty strokes."
Sjoland's triple bogey came at the sixth on his way to a 70 which also included an eagle and five birdies.
While searching for his ball with playing partner Nicolas Vanhootegem of Belgium, Sjoland saw it drop to the ground out of a bush.
When it could not be determined who had disturbed the ball, tournament director David Garland said he had no option but to penalise Sjoland one stroke.
The Swede then added another because his ball had landed in an unplayable lie.
Said Sjoland: "The ball fell out on Vanhootegem's side of the bush but unfortunately I got the penalty.
"...If I had played more years on tour I'd have had the experience to know I shouldn't have touched anything. But this just makes me more determined to win."
He missed a the chance of a playoff in last year's Madeira Open when he five-putted the last green.
